source: NCERT Class XI, India Physical Environment, Ch. 3 (Drainage System).

sections.heading: 1. Drainage — Basics
points: **Drainage** = the flow of water through channels (rivers); a **drainage basin** is the area drained by a river and its tributaries; a **watershed** divides two basins.
**Drainage patterns:** dendritic, radial, trellis, rectangular, centripetal.
Indian rivers are of two groups: **Himalayan** and **Peninsular**.

sections.heading: 2. Himalayan Rivers
points: **Perennial** (fed by snowmelt + rain); long courses; do a lot of erosion; form gorges, meanders, ox-bow lakes, large deltas.
Three main systems: **Indus, Ganga, Brahmaputra**.
**Indus** — rises in Tibet (near Mansarovar); tributaries: Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Satluj (Punjab = 'land of five rivers').
**Ganga** — rises at **Gangotri (Bhagirathi + Alaknanda meet at Devprayag)**; tributaries: Yamuna, Ghaghara, Gandak, Kosi (left); Son (right); Ganga + Brahmaputra form the **Sundarbans delta**.
**Brahmaputra** — rises in Tibet (as Tsangpo); enters India in Arunachal (as Dihang); prone to floods and braiding.

sections.heading: 3. Peninsular Rivers
points: Mostly **seasonal (rain-fed)**; shorter, shallower; flow in fixed courses (old, mature).
**East-flowing (into Bay of Bengal, form deltas):** **Mahanadi, Godavari** ('Dakshin Ganga', largest peninsular river), **Krishna, Kaveri**.
**West-flowing (into Arabian Sea, form estuaries):** **Narmada and Tapi** (flow through rift valleys — no deltas).
The **Western Ghats** form the main water divide of the peninsula.

sections.heading: 4. River Importance and Problems
points: Rivers provide **water, irrigation, hydropower, navigation, fisheries**.
Problems: **pollution** (industrial/sewage), leading to programmes like the **Namami Gange / Ganga Action Plan**.
River water disputes between states (Cauvery, Krishna).

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Himalayan rivers = perennial (snow+rain); Peninsular = seasonal (rain-fed).
Indus tributaries: Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Satluj (Punjab = five rivers).
Ganga = Bhagirathi + Alaknanda (meet at Devprayag); Sundarbans delta with Brahmaputra.
Godavari = largest peninsular river ('Dakshin Ganga').
Narmada & Tapi = west-flowing in rift valleys → estuaries (no delta).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Himalayan rivers are perennial**; **Peninsular rivers are seasonal**.
**Narmada and Tapi flow WEST** through **rift valleys** and form **estuaries** (not deltas).
**Godavari** is the **largest peninsular river** ('Dakshin Ganga').
The **Ganga** is formed at **Devprayag** (Bhagirathi + Alaknanda).
